papers.title: Guest-Assisted Assembled Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Frameworks of Dysprosium Single-Ion Magnets
papers.authors: Bei-Bei Zhang, Song Peng, Shu-Ying Luo, Ning Gao, Qing-Hu Teng, Fu-Pei Liang, Kai Wang
papers.summary: Guest-assisted hydrogen bonding assembles dysprosium single-ion magnets into two- and three-dimensional frameworks. Thermal characterization and magnetic measurements connect robust assemblies with field-induced dual relaxation processes.
papers.whyRelevant: Offers a framework-design comparison for controlling lanthanide magnetic relaxation, without establishing coherent qubit operation.

relatedPapers.reason: Both study lanthanide spins in extended framework environments.

papers.title: Broadband AC magnetic field sensing via continuous wave optically detected magnetic resonance with NV centers in diamond
papers.authors: Ryohei Dokai, Ryusei Okaniwa, Miku Ishizaki, Junko Ishi-Hayase, Yuichiro Matsuzaki
papers.summary: A theoretical CW-ODMR scheme uses microwave-dressed NV states to extend AC magnetometry to substantially higher frequencies. Numerical simulations explore broadband detection beyond the narrow frequency ranges of conventional continuous-wave protocols.
papers.whyRelevant: A practical control concept to compare with pulse-based sensing bandwidth; the reported extension is simulated.

relatedPapers.reason: Both concern the design of quantum-sensor measurement protocols.

papers.title: Nanophotonic quantum magnetometry in a spin-dense diamond cavity
papers.authors: Nicholas J. Sorensen, Elham Zohari, Joshua S. Wildeman, Sigurd Flågan, Vinaya K. Kavatamane, Paul E. Barclay
papers.summary: An integrated diamond cavity containing dense NV centers combines fiber-coupled optical excitation and collection with Ramsey magnetometry. The experiment demonstrates compact, low-power magnetic sensing while retaining micrometer-scale spatial resolution.
papers.whyRelevant: Relevant to optical integration and readout efficiency in dense spin sensors, with a different host platform from molecular frameworks.

relatedPapers.reason: Relevant to optical integration and readout efficiency in dense spin sensors, with a different host platform from molecular frameworks.

papers.title: Phase-accumulating hyperfine strain sensing with rare-earth-ion phase memories
papers.summary: A proposed rare-earth-ion protocol converts strain-induced hyperfine shifts into accumulated phase. Synchronized dynamical decoupling preserves the response to an oscillating strain drive, followed by Raman-heterodyne readout of the stored coherence.
papers.whyRelevant: Closely connects spin–lattice coupling, pulse control and sensing; the paper proposes a protocol rather than demonstrating a finished sensor.

relatedPapers.reason: Closely connects spin–lattice coupling, pulse control and sensing; the paper proposes a protocol rather than demonstrating a finished sensor.

papers.title: Capturing Transient Polaron Formation Dynamics: A Time-Dependent Polaron Transformation Approach
papers.authors: Zeyu Dong, Wenxiang Ying, Feng-Feng Song, Peng Zhang, Hanggai Nuomin
papers.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.archiveJournal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.summary: A time-dependent polaron transformation describes gradual environmental dressing rather than imposing it at the initial time. Benchmarks against numerically exact dynamics show advantages when transient polaron formation competes with the evolution of a dissipative two-level system.
papers.whyRelevant: Directly relevant to nonequilibrium spin–phonon models and the limits of static polaron approximations.

relatedPapers.reason: Directly relevant to nonequilibrium spin–phonon models and the limits of static polaron approximations.

papers.title: Beyond Swelling: Electrochemical Doping Tunes the Balance between Ion Compensation and Exchange in a Hydrated Organic Mixed Ionic–Electronic Conductor
papers.authors: Zixuan Wei, Ying Xiang, Hesam Makki, Wanlin Xu, Xingli Chen, Chao Deng, Sheng Bi, Xiaohui Yang, Yan Sun, Feng Wang, Jianhua Chen, Paola Carbone, Fujie Tang, Alessandro Troisi, Jun Cheng
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.archiveJournal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: Constant-potential simulations examine how electrochemical doping reorganizes polymer, ions and water in an organic mixed conductor. Spectroscopic comparisons support the model, which identifies changing ion-compensation and exchange regimes near the mobility maximum.
papers.whyRelevant: A comparative reference for separating hydration, ionic motion and electronic transport in conductive molecular materials.

relatedPapers.reason: A comparative reference for separating hydration, ionic motion and electronic transport in conductive molecular materials.

papers.title: Thermally enhanced magnon-phonon resonance in van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3
papers.authors: Kai-Xuan Zhang, Beom Hyun Kim, Seungbok Lee, Hao Li, Eugene Park, Heejun Yang, Feng Jin, Qingming Zhang, Je-Geun Park
papers.summary: Temperature-dependent high-field Raman measurements show robust magnon–phonon coupling in FePS3. Warming reduces mode detuning and enhances hybridization near the magnetic transition, offering insight into previously reported driven magnetic states.
papers.whyRelevant: A comparative materials example for spin–lattice hybridization; it does not directly measure molecular-qubit coherence.

relatedPapers.reason: A comparative materials example for spin–lattice hybridization; it does not directly measure molecular-qubit coherence.

papers.title: Bayesian optimization enhanced magnetic field gradient detection based on spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensates
papers.authors: Shixiang Chen, Juan Wang, Yan Li
papers.summary: A proposed spin–orbit-coupled condensate gradiometer maps a magnetic-field gradient onto rotational deflection. Bayesian optimization searches the model’s control parameters and improves the predicted sensitivity relative to the studied baseline.
papers.whyRelevant: An adjacent example of automated sensing-parameter optimization; the proposal is not a molecular-sensor experiment.

relatedPapers.reason: An adjacent example of automated sensing-parameter optimization; the proposal is not a molecular-sensor experiment.

papers.title: Quantum sensing of a weak drive signal in cascaded quantum van der Pol oscillators
papers.summary: A model of cascaded quantum van der Pol oscillators transfers a weak drive from a probe to a separate measurement oscillator. Nonreciprocal coupling and dissipation determine the available precision, with favorable scaling restricted to particular dynamical regimes.
papers.whyRelevant: A theoretical reference on indirect sensing and engineered dissipation, with transfer to molecular-spin systems still speculative.

relatedPapers.reason: A theoretical reference on indirect sensing and engineered dissipation, with transfer to molecular-spin systems still speculative.
